## Start here | You have | Go to | |---|---| | **An Android TV or Google TV** | [Quick start](#quick-start): a coding assistant does the work in about fifteen minutes. | | **A Samsung, LG, Roku, Vizio or Hisense VIDAA TV** | [cleanyour.tv/not-android](https://cleanyour.tv/not-android): CleanYourTV can't run there, but you can turn off the tracking with your remote. | | **Only an Android phone** | The community-built [Clean Your TV app](https://cleanyour.tv/app): no laptop, no coding agent. | | **Want to see it first** | [What you get](#what-you-get): screenshots of the new home screen. | **Official links:** [cleanyour.tv](https://cleanyour.tv) and this repo. Other domains using the name, such as cleanyourtv.com, are not run by this project ([#1004](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/issues/1004)). [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [What you get](#what-you-get) · [Supported TVs](#supported-tvs) · [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) · [The launcher](#the-launcher) · [Restoring](#restoring-your-tv) · [Firmware updates](#after-a-firmware-update) · [Questions](#questions-people-ask) · [Contributing](#contributing) ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: | Step | What happens | |---|---| | **Back up** | The list of installed packages and settings. | | **Disable** | The manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk, with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. | | **Install** | A small native launcher, made the default home screen. | **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.** The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start | You have | Do this | |---|---| | **A computer** | Use the prompt with a coding assistant: the three steps below. | | **A computer, no coding assistant** | Run the three steps yourself: the commands are in [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand). | | **Only an Android phone** | Use the community-built [Clean Your TV app](https://cleanyour.tv/app) by [@udhaykumarbala](https://github.com/udhaykumarbala): connect, analyse, clean, in about five minutes. No laptop, no coding agent. | The three steps below are written for a coding assistant: the computer needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV, with a shell on it, plus Python 3, a JDK from 17 through 22, and Android SDK platform 34 with build-tools 34 (the assistant builds the launcher there). Without an assistant, [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) is the same job, run by you, and it has the install commands. Any of these work: Claude Code (on [0G Private Computer](https://pc.0g.ai/?utm_source=cleanyourtv&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme) or an [Anthropic plan](https://claude.com/pricing)), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) or [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli). | Where | What to do | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. | | **2. On your computer** | Clone the repo and open that folder in your assistant (`git clone https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv`), then paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) and fill in your TV model. | | **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, the dock size and app order, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. | Cloning matters: the assistant reuses this repo's `tools/disable.sh` and `launcher/build-and-install.sh` instead of writing its own, and that is where the backup, the Home guard and the restore record live. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes. ## What you get A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way: | Part | What it looks like | |---|---| | **A pitch-black home** | A dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. | | **A top shelf** | Names the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. | | **The rest of your apps in a grid** | Slides up when you press Down. | | **One floating glass highlight** | Springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. | | **Three frosted buttons** | Inputs (HDMI ports under the names you gave them in the TV's settings, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. | | **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** | In [Outfit](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Outfit), and a matching Clock screensaver. Set `show_stats` in config or a theme for one line under the clock: CPU, free memory and free storage. It stays off unless you turn it on, and it refreshes only while Home is on screen. | | **Themes and module cards** | Themes change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and module cards let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. | And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. | | | |---|---| | ![The top shelf names the focused app over an ambient glow in its colour](docs/focus-2-up-netflix.png) | ![The Inputs popup: HDMI ports with what is connected, AV and Live TV](docs/inputs-menu.jpg) | | *Top shelf and ambient glow* | *Inputs: HDMI with connection state, AV, Live TV* | | ![The grid with the glass highlight on a tile and its name beneath](docs/focus-1-fancode.png) | ![The Clock screensaver: a thin clock drifting over the glow](docs/clock-screensaver.png) | | *The grid, one glass highlight, the tile's name* | *Clock screensaver, drifts so nothing burns in* | | ![The aurora theme: a wallpaper and tinted pills, pushed without a rebuild](themes/aurora/screenshot.jpg) | ![Six columns and a six-app dock from a theme's config.json](themes/six-columns/screenshot.jpg) | | *Aurora theme, pushed with `tools/theme.sh`* | *Six columns and a six-app dock, same launcher* | | ![Moving a tile: held OK, chose Move, the tile is picked up and the others dim](docs/tile-move.jpg) | ![The App library: installed apps, one press adds an app back to Home](docs/app-library.jpg) | | *With `tile_menu`, hold OK on a tile, Move: arrows carry it, Back puts it down* | *App library: one press puts a removed app back on Home* | ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**. | Platform | What works | |---|---| | **Android TV, Google TV** | The debloat and the launcher. | | **Fire TV** | The debloat half only, since Fire OS will not hand Home to a third-party launcher. And on the 2015 Fire TV Box (Fire OS 5) even that half fails: every `pm` route is refused. | | **A few China-market TCL sets** | They refuse to install any launcher at all; their lists say so in the header. | | **Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS), Roku, Vizio, Hisense VIDAA** | Not supported (no ADB). Turn off the tracking instead: [cleanyour.tv/not-android](https://cleanyour.tv/not-android). See [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md#other-platforms-fire-tv-and-lg-webos) for four webOS ports, and [docs/devices/samsung-tizen.md](docs/devices/samsung-tizen.md) for what a 2021 Samsung set answers over Wi-Fi (no ADB, so no `pm disable-user`) if you are weighing a Tizen port. | Tested lists from contributors, one folder per model in [`examples/`](examples/). Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. Two things have to be on the computer first: | You need | For | |---|---| | **Python 3** (any 3.x) | The tools. The venv command below installs what they import. | | **JDK 17 through 22** (a full JDK, including `jlink`) and **Android SDK platform 34** with **build-tools 34.0.0 or any newer 34.x** | Building the launcher. JDK 23 and newer stops Gradle 8.9. Platform 34 is the one the build reads; a newer platform does not replace it. On macOS, when none of these is installed: `brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools`, then `sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0"`. On Linux the install script looks in `~/Android/Sdk` and for `java` on your PATH. | `tools/tv.py` talks to network ADB on port 5555. If that port stays closed and the TV offers Wireless debugging with a pairing code (the Chromecast with Google TV and the Google TV Streamer do), pair it once with the stock `adb` and run `adb tcpip 5555` first, as [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#connecting) describes. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # one shell command on the TV tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it, stock launcher back tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/check.py examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # what a firmware update undid TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh # build the launcher and make it Home tools/theme.sh themes/aurora # push a theme; --reset removes it ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull, reboot, and screenshots, optionally pressing remote keys first. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. Optional [paired Google ADB backend](tools/native-adb.md) for encrypted Wireless debugging. | | [`tools/docker-build.sh`](tools/docker-build.sh) | Builds the launcher or an add-on in Docker (JDK 17, Android SDK 34), so this computer needs nothing but Docker. Install the result with `SKIP_BUILD=1`. [Guide](tools/docker-build.md). | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads large files such as APKs in base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/relay.py`](tools/relay.py) | Forwards a local port to the TV's ADB port, for assistants whose sandbox can't reach your network. Listens on this computer only. [Guide](tools/relay.md). | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list, the undo from the state recorded before the change. | | [`tools/recovery.py`](tools/recovery.py) | Writes the record `disable.sh` needs to undo itself, and prints the restore batch. | | [`tools/check.py`](tools/check.py) | Compares the TV with the list that was applied, for what a firmware update undid; `--fix` puts it back. | | [`tools/adb-closed.py`](tools/adb-closed.py) | Checks that the TV's network ADB port is closed once debugging is off: exits 0 when the TV refuses the connection, 1 while it is still open, 2 when nothing answered or the check itself could not run. No `nc` needed. | | [`tools/privacy.py`](tools/privacy.py) | Audits the TV for voice, ACR and telemetry candidates and prints the evidence for each; `--write` turns the findings into a list `disable.sh` and `restore.sh` already understand. | | [`tools/theme.sh`](tools/theme.sh), [`theme_restart.py`](tools/theme_restart.py) | Push a folder from [`themes/`](themes/) to the launcher and restart Home. | | [`tools/manage.py`](tools/manage.py) | List every add-on, theme and switch with its screenshot, see what is on the TV, and install, update or remove one by running its creator's own script. | | [`tools/bench.py`](tools/bench.py) | Measures the launcher that answers HOME: key latency, how far the focus moved, janky frames, cold start, return to Home, and the idle CPU and PSS it costs. Changes nothing on the TV and writes the raw per-key numbers to JSON; no extra install. | | [`tools/trace.py`](tools/trace.py), [`trace_report.py`](tools/trace_report.py) | Records Perfetto traces of the launcher (return to Home, cold start, D-pad) and reports where its time goes, per run and before against after. Optional: needs [`requirements-perf.txt`](tools/requirements-perf.txt). [Guide](tools/trace.md). | | [`tools/flamechart.py`](tools/flamechart.py) | Draws a before/after flame chart from those traces, for a pull request: one lane per thread on a shared time scale, the work a change targets in magenta with its total. Optional, like the trace tools. [Guide](tools/flamechart.md). | | [`tools/screendiff.py`](tools/screendiff.py) | Compares a before and an after screenshot pixel by pixel, leaving out the clock or anything you mask, and writes the pair with your Wi-Fi name blurred. Optional, like the trace tools. [Guide](tools/screendiff.md). | | [`tools/race_calendar.py`](tools/race_calendar.py) | Writes this season's F1 calendar into a theme for race-weekend mode, from the free Jolpica API. | | [`launcher/build-and-install.sh`](launcher/build-and-install.sh) | Builds a shrunk release (about 561 KB), installs it, switches Home, and rolls back if Home does not land on it. | The scripts never leave the TV without a Home app: they only disable a stock launcher they recognise, and skip the Home app in a list until another launcher answers HOME. Your own lists can live outside the repository: list paths are relative to the directory you run from, and absolute paths work too.
Windows (PowerShell) Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. Install Python 3 and a JDK from 17 through 22, and in the SDK Manager add platform 34 and build-tools 34 (34.0.0 or any newer 34.x). The script uses `JAVA_HOME` when it points at a JDK in that range, and otherwise Android Studio's bundled JDK when that JDK is in the same range: ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\theme.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 themes\aurora ``` The last two are the undo and a theme push, the `tools/restore.sh` and `tools/theme.sh` lines the sections above give in bash. On Google TV the undo takes the stock launcher as well: `-Stock com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`.
How the scripts protect Home The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise, the four in `KNOWN_STOCK_LAUNCHERS`: `com.google.android.tvlauncher`, `com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`, `com.google.android.leanbacklauncher` and Xiaomi's `com.mitv.tvhome` (PatchWall). Pass `STOCK_LAUNCHER=` (`-StockLauncher`) to override, or `none` to leave it alone. `tools/disable.sh` (`disable.ps1`) applies the same rule before it disables anything: - If the list contains the app that owns Home and no other app on the TV answers HOME, it skips that entry, says why, and disables the rest of the list. So a list applied before the launcher handover cannot leave the TV with nothing to start. - The setup wizard, the settings apps, a vendor `FallbackHome` and factory-test apps (Xiaomi's `com.duokan.factorytest`) answer HOME too and don't count. - On Google TV it also keeps the owner while setupwraith answers HOME and stays enabled (not listed, or kept for the Wi-Fi network): setupwraith answers ahead of an installed launcher that is not Home yet, so it would take Home. Run the same list again once `launcher/build-and-install.sh` has made the new launcher Home and the entry is applied; `FORCE_HOME=1` (`$env:FORCE_HOME`) disables it anyway.
## The microphone, and what can be said about it "Which of these packages is listening?" has no honest one-line answer: a permission scan shows fifty system packages with `RECORD_AUDIO` that record nothing, and ACR clients see the screen with no audio permission at all. [`tools/privacy.py`](tools/privacy.py) reports what the TV actually says, with the evidence for each voice, ACR and telemetry candidate: `TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/privacy.py`, and `--write` turns them into a normal debloat list. What the audit cannot do is prove intent: [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md) explains why. ## The launcher A small native home screen for Android TV: **about 561 KB**, plain Java, built for TVs with 1 GB of RAM. No blur, no video, no network permission, no background services. The **TV** needs Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer, the `minSdk` in [`launcher/app/build.gradle`](launcher/app/build.gradle); what is left on an older set is in [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). | What | How it works | |---|---| | **Configure** | Dock order, hidden apps, Live TV app, 4 to 7 tiles per row, reduced motion. All in [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml) | | **Settings on the TV** | Hold OK on Settings for launcher settings. Optional `launcher_settings_button` makes a normal click open them directly; TV settings remain on the settings page and their app tile. | | **Themes** | Background, wallpaper and layout from a `config.json` pushed over Wi-Fi, no rebuild. twelve ship in [`themes/`](themes/), the built-in `default/` included | | **30 languages** | Follows the TV's language, with a fully mirrored right-to-left layout for Hebrew | | **App library** | Optional: browse every installed app and add or remove Home shortcuts. See [the app library guide](docs/app-library.md) | | **Tile menu** | Optional (`tile_menu`): hold OK on a tile for Move, Remove from Home and App info. Off, holding OK opens App info | | **Module cards** | Any TV app can offer its own tile; you approve each one once. See [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md) | | **Add-ons** | Optional apps that plug in as module cards, kept in [`addons/`](addons/) and never built into the launcher | | **Clock screensaver** | A drifting clock over the glow, so nothing burns in | | **Remote keys** | Keeps the Input, YouTube and gear buttons working after the stock launcher is gone | Themes, switches and add-ons together, with screenshots: [cleanyour.tv/addons](https://cleanyour.tv/addons). **More:** [docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md) has the launcher settings page row by row, changing the default home, the languages, remote keys, the Clock screensaver, navigation and building it yourself. ## Restoring your TV Keep the list you applied. One line puts the TV back the way it was: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt # Android TV TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx # Google TV ``` | What | How | |---|---| | **A record comes first** | Before `tools/disable.sh` changes anything it writes down what the TV looked like, in `~/.cleanyourtv/`. | | **Restore replays it** | A package you had disabled yourself stays disabled, and Home goes back to the component that owned it. | | **The launcher stays installed** | Remove it from the TV's Settings → Apps if you want it gone. | | **No computer?** | If the TV is unreachable, its own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages too. | **More:** [docs/restore.md](docs/restore.md) has what the record holds, when the stock launcher argument counts, and what happens without a record. ## After a firmware update An update installs over the cleaned-up system: the listed packages come back, Home goes to the stock launcher, and new preloads appear that no list mentions. Open ADB again as in [Quick start](#quick-start) step 1, then compare the TV with the list you applied; `--fix` puts it back: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/check.py examples//debloat.txt ``` **More:** [docs/firmware-updates.md](docs/firmware-updates.md) has the exit codes, a weekly check, what `--fix` changes, TVs that keep the stock launcher as Home, and lists that disable the updater. ## When something goes wrong The full list of things that bit us is in [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). The three that matter most: - 🍎 **macOS blocks `adb connect`** ("No route to host") under Local Network privacy. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary. - ⚠️ **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed and running**, or Home lands on a factory test app. The install script orders this for you. - 🔁 **On Google TV the setup wizard** (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) can take Home and crash-loop the system after the stock launcher is disabled. Disable it too, and list it in your `debloat.txt` so restore brings it back. - But check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` first: if the Wi-Fi network was saved during setup it belongs to setupwraith, and disabling it deletes the network (re-join it in Settings first; `tools/disable.sh` skips setupwraith until you do). - On Google's own Chromecast and on the Google TV Streamer it also costs phone casting, see [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). - Stuck already? `tools/tv.py 'pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx'`. ## Questions people ask
I don't code and don't have a laptop. Can I still do this? Yes. [@udhaykumarbala](https://github.com/udhaykumarbala) built a free, open-source [phone app](https://cleanyour.tv/app) for Android that does the same cleanup over Wi-Fi: it connects to the TV, shows a plan first, saves a restore point, and only switches apps off, so everything can be put back. It's community-built.
Is this safe? Can it brick the TV? Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted; packages are disabled in the user profile. The risk is disabling something the TV leans on, which is why lists are applied in small batches with a restore script ready. The TV's own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages even without the tools. If the TV no longer starts far enough for that, a factory reset from its recovery menu is usually the way back. More: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#is-this-safe-can-it-brick-the-tv)
What about firmware updates? The updater is left on in most lists, so firmware updates arrive as usual. Some lists disable the TV's own updater, and on those a firmware update arrives only when you re-enable it. When one does land it installs over the cleaned-up system, so a package comes back and you re-run the script: see [After a firmware update](#after-a-firmware-update).
Won't the apps break? Streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher just lists what is installed and launches it with intents that have been stable for a decade.
Can I do this for someone in another home? Yes, over a private [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) link instead of the same Wi-Fi: either Tailscale on their TV, shared with you, or a computer or Apple TV at their home routing to it. Never by opening the ADB port on their router. Step by step in [docs/REMOTE.md](docs/REMOTE.md).
Isn't ADB access a security hole? It is one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. Network ADB is plaintext on port 5555, and on some firmware any device on the LAN gets a shell, so close it when you are done: 1. On the TV: Developer options → turn **USB debugging**, **Network/ADB debugging** and **Wireless debugging** off, whichever the TV has, and revoke the USB debugging authorisations. 2. Reboot the TV, then confirm the port is gone from your computer: `python3 tools/adb-closed.py ` must say the port is closed. The launcher keeps working without debugging. More, including checking Wireless debugging's own port: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#isnt-adb-access-a-security-hole)
Can it block ads inside apps too? Partly, with Android's Private DNS (Android 9 and newer). Point it at an ad-blocking resolver such as [AdGuard DNS](https://adguard-dns.io) and every app's ad and tracker domains stop resolving, system-wide, surviving reboots. The trade-off: that resolver then sees every DNS query the TV makes, and it does not remove YouTube ads. More, with the two commands and how to switch back: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#can-it-block-ads-inside-apps-too)
Are there switches in the TV's own Settings worth flipping too? A few, and they need no ADB: the advertising ID, Location, Usage & diagnostics and Scanning always available, plus Apps only mode where the stock launcher stays. Flip Usage & diagnostics before the debloat; on some TVs its page goes with it. More, with the paths for Google TV, Android TV and Fire OS: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#are-there-switches-in-the-tvs-own-settings-worth-flipping-too)
AirPlay? Not from this repo. Chromecast built-in stays for Android phones. For iPhones, [jqssun/android-airplay-server](https://github.com/jqssun/android-airplay-server) works; an install script for it is in [PR #84](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/pull/84).
Can I just download the APK? Build it with the one-line script in [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand); it takes a minute and you control what goes on your TV. That needs the JDK and Android SDK named there. No prebuilt binaries.
## The story On 17 October 2026 I posted [a before and after](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102) of my parents' TV, cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi. It reached 7.4M views, people started doing the same to their own TVs, and their replies turned into the lists here: 170+ TV models from 200+ contributors in four days. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. The coverage since is in [docs/PRESS.md](docs/PRESS.md). ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model does not have to rediscover it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the format and the testing we ask for. Contributing through a coding agent? [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) gives it the same rules. | How to help | What it means | |---|---| | **Your TV's debloat list** | The most useful one: the next person with that model skips the discovery. | | **Launcher and prompt** | Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. | | **Built something on top?** | A launcher, a port, a theme: add it to [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md), where a hundred and fifty-one projects already live, sorted into home screens, forks, add-ons, tools and other platforms, with an index by TV brand. | The people whose work is in this repo:
Star history
## Contact | For | Where | |---|---| | **Questions about your TV** | [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/discussions) | | **Press and queries** | [hello@itsgathin.com](mailto:hello@itsgathin.com) | | **Security issues** | Report them privately through the [Security tab](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/security), see [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | ## Legal - CleanYourTV is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any TV maker or platform. Brand and model names are used only to say which TV a list was tested on, and remain the trademarks of their owners. - It works only through settings the TV itself offers to its owner: Developer options, ADB debugging and Android's own `pm disable-user`, the same switch as Settings > Apps > Disable. It does not root the TV, flash firmware, or bypass any lock, DRM or copy protection, and the repo contains no manufacturer software, firmware or APKs. - Nothing is uninstalled, and `tools/restore.sh` puts everything back. title: Zagitta/gpu-unlock
author: Zagitta
body:
![gpu-unlock: full-speed tensor cores for GeForce RTX](assets/banner.svg)

### Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it.

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-76b900)![RTX 20 | 30 | 40](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-RTX%2020%20%7C%2030%20%7C%2040-76b900?logo=nvidia&logoColor=white)![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux-informational?logo=linux&logoColor=white)![License GPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Zagitta/gpu-unlock?style=flat&color=yellow)

**Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput** · **+25–55% LLM prefill** · **+25–50% fine-tuning** · **+30–55% image generation**

[Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus) · [Benchmarks](#what-you-get) · [Install](#how-to-install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Support](#support-me)

---

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

---

## What you get

The tensor core rate doubles. How much of that you see depends on how much of
your workload is FP16/BF16/TF32 matrix math, and on whether the card has the
power headroom to run it.

Dense matrix multiply (FP32 accumulation, stock power limits):

| Card | BF16 before | BF16 after | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12 GB | 27 TFLOPS | 51 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 3060 Ti | 37 TFLOPS | 68 TFLOPS | +82% |
| RTX 3070 | 40 TFLOPS | 72 TFLOPS | +81% |
| RTX 3080 10 GB | 65 TFLOPS | 113 TFLOPS | +73% |
| RTX 3090 | 75 TFLOPS | 125 TFLOPS | +65% |
| RTX 3090 Ti (450 W) | 88 TFLOPS | 157 TFLOPS | +80% |
| RTX 4070 Ti | 81 TFLOPS | 150 TFLOPS | +84% |
| RTX 4080 | 104 TFLOPS | 193 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 4090 | 165 TFLOPS | 329 TFLOPS | +100% (peak MMA rate) |

The RTX 4090 runs out of power before it runs out of tensor cores, so large
GEMMs at stock power limits gain much less than the peak rate suggests.

Real workloads:

| Workload | Typical speedup |
| --- | --- |
| LLM prefill / prompt processing, FP16/BF16 or AWQ/GPTQ (vLLM, PyTorch, Transformers) | +25–55% |
| Time to first token | 25–30% lower |
| LoRA and full fine-tuning in BF16 | +25–50% |
| Image generation, FP16/BF16 (SDXL, SD 1.5, Krea, DiT models in ComfyUI) | +30–55% |
| Video generation, BF16 compute (Wan 2.2) | +15–20% |
| FlashAttention / SDPA kernels | +50–60% |
| llama.cpp / Ollama with quantized GGUF | 0–15%, mostly at long context |
| LLM decode / token generation (memory bound) | No change |
| INT8, FP8 and INT4 models | No change |
| Gaming and FP32 CUDA | No change |

Outputs are bit-identical before and after; only the speed changes. These
numbers come from the [compatibility reports](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues)
users have filed, where you can find full benchmark details and post your own.

---

## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping
existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`
in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run
`sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run
`sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.
- **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in your boot entry
(`bootctl status` shows its location).
- **UKI / generated entries:** add it to `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and regenerate
your boot images/entries (e.g. `sudo mkinitcpio -P` for mkinitcpio UKIs).

# FAQ

- Q: Do you have a website/coin/installer?  
A: No this is the one and only OG source for gpu-unlock. Crypto, websites, installers and what else is not associated with this project or the developer in any way shape or form. 
- Q: Does this depend on a specific driver version? I see `610.43.03` is pinned.  
A: No the driver is only fetched to extract firmware this unlock depends on    
- Q: What about Windows?  
A: I don't run windows and don't plan to maintain it but [https://github.com/impacifist/Windows-GPU-UNLOCK](https://github.com/impacifist/Windows-GPU-UNLOCK) has built a port, YMMV.   
There are windows installer's floating around but I would recommend being ++**very**++ careful with those.
- Q: What about Blackwell (RTX 50)?  
A: Not supported and unlikely to happen.    
- Q: Why did Nvidia handicap my GPU?  
A: Market segmentation, they want businesses to purchase the professional cards without these limitations at significantly higher prices.
- Q: Does this hurt my GPU?  
A: It's very unlikely, this only unlocks a small handicap Nvidia has put in place to differentiate datacenter and professional cards from consumer versions. It may heat up your GPU slightly because it now does more compute but the standard throttling and power management remains completely intact and should downclock.    
- Q: How can I assist?  
A: Please consider [donating](#support-me) so I can purchase more GPUs <3

## Local build

Every build downloads the NVIDIA/CachyOS inputs over HTTPS and generates
firmware only in the build directory and the binary package. All three formats install through the same `make install-*`
targets. Packages are built from the working tree, uncommitted changes included.

Build, install build dependencies, and install the packages in one step
(asks for your sudo password):

```sh
make install        # detect the distribution and select an installer
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make install` uses `/etc/os-release` (`ID`, then `ID_LIKE`) to detect Arch,
Debian/Ubuntu, or Fedora/RHEL/CentOS families. The RPM installer requires DNF.
For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` only build. Debian and RPM packages go
to `build/deb` and `build/rpm`. The NVIDIA inputs are cached in
`~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs` (`make inputs`; override with `INPUTS=`).
`dpkg-buildpackage` itself never uses the network, so a clean-chroot build (sbuild or
pbuilder) needs `GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing at that cache.
The `make dist` archive, the Debian source package and the `.nosrc.rpm`
contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware.

## How it works

This Linux kernel module combines the cmpunlocker's V67/PLM technique with the
pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. At boot it runs the unlock, writes the
speed selectors (SS0 `0x88888888`, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the
4-bit SS1 `0x8` IMLA4) and performs an FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver
binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver.

## Boot flow and opt-in

The packages put `gpu_unlock` and its firmware in the initramfs and load it
there, before `nvidia` can bind a card:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` inserts
`gpu_unlock` right before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, so a display card is blank
for as short a time as possible. Without `nvidia` in the image, it goes
last and still runs before an `nvidia` loaded from the root filesystem.
Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image
built with `-c <config>` or a preset `_config`; put `gpu_unlock` right
before `nvidia` in that config's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:** `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed
kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install
and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new
image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule: kmod honours only the first
`softdep nvidia` line it reads, so other packages' rules (`nvidia-utils`,
`gddr6_hwmon`) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

```
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every supported unbound card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated
```

Addresses are full PCI names as `lspci -D` prints them (hex digits in either
case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not
a supported card (see [Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus)), including `all` mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored.
The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many
there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered
down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro
X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared
first; a card some driver already initialised is still refused. Then
`nvidia` loads and binds every card as usual.

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and
Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is
removed just before the card's reset, as `nvidia-drm` would do a moment
later anyway. Its screen is blank from that reset until `nvidia-drm` takes
over.

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that `nvidia`
has bound.

Suspend to RAM powers the cards off, which resets the speed selectors. After
resume the module unlocks every card it unlocked at boot again, before
`nvidia` resumes it: its suspend notifier runs just ahead of the one `nvidia`
resumes its cards from (`NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1`, the default in
current drivers; `nvidia-resume.service` runs later still). This adds about a
second to resume. A card that kept power, as in suspend to idle, is still
unlocked and is only read. A card that `nvidia` has already resumed, or that is
bound to another driver, is left as it is, and the log says why. Add
`gpu_unlock.resume=0` to the kernel command line, or write `0` to
`/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume`, to turn this off. Hibernation is
not covered.

Check the result with:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:[ID]:00.0
```

To stop unlocking, remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line;
for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the
packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA
buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off
before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated buffer
derives from the pinned CMP reference; NVIDIA firmware remains under its own
terms. See `firmware/NOTICE.md` and `licenses/` for attribution and notices.

title: simbasjungles/free-my-tv
author: simbasjungles
body:
# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour (up to six, in Home Settings) from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have, and from the services you choose. The focused one opens wide and the others show their posters. Movies and Shows get their own tabs, and on Google TV your own [Plex library](#your-plex-library-optional) can join in. - **Continue Watching** (Google TV and Android TV). *Home Settings* → *Top of the screen* puts what you left halfway in your apps on top, with its progress, and OK picks it up in its app. Or a big clock, or the picks. - **Your TMDB key from your phone.** *Home Settings* → *TMDB key* shows a QR code: scan it and paste the key. On LG and Samsung, type it with the remote. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast (or the next 5 days), sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **What's playing.** Music, a podcast or the radio going on in the background shows on the home screen and the screensaver: the title, the artist and the app, from any app that tells Android what it plays (*Home Settings*, off until you turn it on). - **The status at a glance, and a mouse** (Google TV and Android TV). *Home Settings* → *Status icons* puts Wi-Fi or Ethernet, Bluetooth audio and a USB drive at the top of the home screen; off, nothing listens for them. A mouse or an air-mouse remote works too: hover moves the focus, the wheel scrolls, a click picks. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. On LG and Samsung, *Home Settings* → *Screensaver* can make it a large clock with the weather instead, drifting slowly so it doesn't burn into OLED screens. Optionally (*Watch from the screensaver*, in Home Settings), OK opens the title on screen in its app, and any other button just closes it. - **Dimming for a dark room** (LG and Samsung). *Home Settings* → *Dim* darkens Free My TV's own screens, not the apps you open: low, medium, high, or automatic (medium from 22:00 to 07:00). Off until you pick it. - **Your own photos** (Google TV and Android TV). Send them from your computer (up to 100): the screensaver shows them, and without picks one is the home screen's background each hour. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, how many picks and which streaming services they come from, the weather and prices cards, the forecast's hours or days, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 8 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. The APK goes on the TV, not on your phone (on a phone, the settings say so and nothing switches). ### The easy way: an AI assistant 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, open an AI coding assistant ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Codex or Antigravity) and say: > Install Free My TV (github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv) on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It downloads the code, installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV, and asks before anything important. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 3. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. That's when the TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* for Free My TV: tick *Always allow* and accept. ### The ready APK No tools to install besides adb. The APK on the [latest release](https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv/releases/latest) has no TMDB key: add yours on the TV for the picks (*Home Settings* → *TMDB key*, [below](#the-tmdb-key)). It takes your city from the TV's time zone (change it in *Home Settings* → *City*). If you built Free My TV yourself before, switch back to *Original* and uninstall it first: your build and the release are signed with different keys. 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **On your computer**, download `FreeMyTV.apk` from the release and install it: ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555 adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk ``` On Android 14, Google Play Protect may hold the install with *Risky app blocked*: choose *More details* → *Install anyway*. Install it with adb like this, not by opening the APK on the TV: from a file manager or a browser, Play Protect can refuse it outright with *App blocked to protect your device* (in some countries it blocks sideloaded apps that have an accessibility service or a notification listener, which Free My TV uses for the remote's buttons and Now Playing; #378). On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts). An uninstall takes the permission back, so run it again after every new install: ```bash adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow" ``` 3. **On the TV**, do step 3 above. For the picks, add your TMDB key in *Home Settings* → *TMDB key* (below). **Updates come to the TV.** Once a week the APK from the release looks for a newer release and downloads it; the home screen then says so once, and *Home Settings* → *Updates* (the last row) installs it through Android's installer, which asks first (and, the first time, asks to allow Free My TV to install apps). OK on *Updates* also checks right away. The download must come from this repository's releases, match the size and SHA-256 GitHub lists, be newer, and be signed with the project's key. A build you made yourself checks only when you press *Updates*, and only says when a new version is out: build it again to update. ### The manual way 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. On a Mac: ```bash brew install --cask temurin android-commandlinetools android-platform-tools sdkmanager "build-tools;34.0.0" "platforms;android-34" ``` On Linux, get OpenJDK 17, Android's command-line tools and adb from your package manager, then run the same `sdkmanager` line. On Windows, use Git Bash (which Claude Code uses there) or WSL. 3. **Build:** ```bash ./build.sh ``` The first run creates `config.properties`. Set your city and your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key) there, then run it again. 4. **Install:** ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555 adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk ``` If the install seems stuck, look at the TV: on Android 14, Google Play Protect may hold it with *Risky app blocked* ("built for an older version of Android"), since Free My TV targets Android 13. Choose *More details* → *Install anyway*. Updates don't ask again. Chromecast with Google TV on Android 14 keeps port 5555 closed even with USB debugging on: turn on *Wireless debugging* (Developer options), pair with `adb pair `, then run `adb tcpip 5555` over that connection. Port 5555 closes again at every restart, so after one, *Original*, the watchdog and the boot check can't reach ADB until you run `adb tcpip 5555` again (the pairing stays). On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts). An uninstall takes the permission back, so run it again after every new install: ```bash adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow" ``` 5. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. The TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* once more, now for Free My TV itself: tick *Always allow* and accept. (Run `adb disconnect 192.168.1.50:5555` first: on Android 8 to 10 the TV can hand that answer to a computer that's still connected.) On some TCL TVs (Android 11, Realtek), a second background killer, TGuard, can stop the switch while it measures the original home screen: the settings screen closes and the TV's own home screen stays. Android runs the switch again by itself within a minute or two; then press Home: Free My TV opening means it went through. ## LG TVs (webOS) The same home screen as an LG app: the picks, the glass shelf with your apps, the drawer with inputs, weather and prices, day and night, Home Settings and the shelf editor. It installs through LG's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV. LG's home screen stays where it is, and Free My TV is one press of a number key away (or in LG's app list, on remotes without them). You need an LG TV (webOS 3 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with Python 3. 1. **On the TV**, open the LG Content Store and install **Developer Mode**. Sign in with a free [LG developer account](https://webostv.developer.lge.com), turn on **Dev Mode Status** (the TV restarts), then turn on **Key Server**. Write down the IP address and the passphrase it shows. 2. **On your computer**, get the code and build. `config.properties` works as for Google TV (your city, your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv python3 webos/build.py ``` 3. **Install.** The first time, it asks for the TV's passphrase; updates don't: ```bash python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 ``` 4. **On the TV**, while Free My TV is open, hold a number key on the remote. From then on, that key opens it from anywhere. Portuguese, Spanish, German, Russian, Thai and Turkish were translated by hand and are the reference (fix them by hand); the others were machine-made, and corrections from native speakers are welcome. - **Add a language:** `python3 tools/translate.py --new ca`, then fill `app/assets/i18n/ca.json` by hand, or with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, `python3 tools/translate.py --fill --lang ca` (only the strings go to the API). - **After changing text in the code:** `python3 tools/translate.py` lists what each language lacks; `--fill` translates only that (the hand-translated ones, Portuguese, Spanish, German, Russian, Thai and Turkish, are left for a person unless `--lang` names them), `--prune` drops strings the code no longer uses. Run `python3 tools/translate.py --check` to validate all catalogues without writing files. - Text built at runtime has placeholders (`"{n} min ago"`), so each language puts the words in its own order. A key like `"unit|Automatic"` is the same English in another place, where a language may need another word. - Counts have plural forms: `"plural|one:{n} season|other:{n} seasons"` is translated with one form per plural category the language uses (Russian `"one:{n} сезон|few:{n} сезона|many:{n} сезонов|other:{n} сезона"`, Japanese just `"other:{n}シーズン"`), and Android's plural rules pick the one for each number. - **Limits:** right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian) would need the layout mirrored, so they aren't there yet. Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Hindi are drawn with the TV's system font (Inter has no such letters). ## Privacy No accounts, no analytics, no tracking. The app talks to TMDB, Open-Meteo (with the coordinates you set, or your time zone's main city), and Binance only when `show_crypto=true`, Watchmode only when you set a `watchmode_key`, your Plex server only when you set a `plex_url`, your Immich server only when you set one, and Trakt (api.trakt.tv) only when you set a `trakt_client_id` and sign in on the TV. On Google TV and Android TV, the APK from the release asks GitHub (api.github.com) once a week, or when you press *Updates*, for the latest release, and when there's a newer one downloads it from github.com and GitHub's download server (release-assets.githubusercontent.com); a build you made yourself asks only when you press *Updates*. The *Now Playing widget* reads what apps are playing (title, artist, the app) through a notification listener, the only way Android shares it: Free My TV allows the listener only while the widget is on, never reads a notification with it, and asks Android to unbind it as soon as it connects, so it stays unbound. What's playing never leaves the TV. While *Home Settings* → *TMDB key* shows its QR code (5 minutes at most), the TV answers on your home network at that code's address, for one key; the key goes to TMDB only, to check it. Continue Watching (Home Settings) reads what your apps note on the TV itself and shows only pictures already on the TV: it downloads nothing. *Home Settings* → *Status icons* reads only whether the TV has Wi-Fi or Ethernet, a Bluetooth audio device and a mounted USB drive, and only while the row is on: on Android 12 and newer it asks for *Nearby devices* (BLUETOOTH_CONNECT) for the Bluetooth part, and none of it leaves the TV. Your settings stay on your computer and your TV. ## Credits - Built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). - The LG version builds on what [@danielthejoker18](https://github.com/danielthejoker18) found in [FreeMyTvWebOS](https://github.com/danielthejoker18/FreeMyTvWebOS) (MIT): installing through Developer Mode and opening apps through the TV's service bus. - On Samsung TVs it installs with [TizenBrew Installer](https://github.com/reisxd/TizenBrewInstaller) by [@reisxd](https://github.com/reisxd). - This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by [TMDB](https://www.themoviedb.org/). - Links to the titles in the streaming apps by [Watchmode](https://api.watchmode.com/). - Weather data by [Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/) (CC BY 4.0). Prices from the [Binance](https://www.binance.com/) public API. - Icons: [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) (Apache 2.0). Font: [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) (SIL OFL 1.1). Coin logos: [cryptocurrency-icons](https://github.com/spothq/cryptocurrency-icons) (CC0). Samsung app logos: [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) (CC0). - The QR code encoder follows Project Nayuki's [QR Code generator](https://www.nayuki.io/page/qr-code-generator-library) (MIT). - Not affiliated with Google, TCL, LG, Samsung or any streaming service. App names and logos belong to their owners. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Fork it, change it, ship it.

title: Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
author: Jakeschincariol
body:
# The Replica skill

Eleven Claude skills that clone any app. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key,
nothing to connect.

One reverse-engineers the app you want to clone. One rebuilds it. One tests it
for bugs. And one is the Entrepreneur: it reads what the app's users hate and
fixes it in yours, so you have an app you can sell.

In between, the others plan the stack and the database, rebuild the design
system, wire up auth and payments, score your clone against the original, give
it a name and a brand of its own, write the landing page and the store
listing, and put it live on your domain.

**It rebuilds what an app does, never what it owns.** Features and flows,
clean-room style. Not its code, its logo, its copy or its content. The
fine print is at the bottom, and the skills enforce it.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
/plugin install replica-skill@replica-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/replica-skill:replica-recon` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/replica-recon`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.git
cp -r replica-skill/replica-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the
method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/replica-recon` | Reverse-engineers any app: screens, flows, components, data model. From public pages, screenshots, store listings and your own account. |
| `/replica-architect` | Plans the stack, database schema and API for your clone. |
| `/replica-design` | Rebuilds the design system: colours, type, spacing, components. As tokens, with your own assets. |
| `/replica-build` | Rebuilds the app screen by screen from the recon map. |
| `/replica-backend` | Auth, database, payments and integrations. |
| `/replica-test` | Clicks through every flow and tests it for bugs. |
| `/replica-diff` | Compares your clone against the original. A parity score and what is missing. |
| `/replica-entrepreneur` | Reads what the app's users hate in real reviews and turns it into fixes and a positioning angle. |
| `/replica-brand` | Names and rebrands your version so it is yours. |
| `/replica-launch` | Landing page, pricing and App Store listing. |
| `/replica-deploy` | Ships it live on your own domain. |

## How to use it

Run them in order. Each one reads what the last one wrote, in a `replica/`
folder in your project.

```
recon -> architect -> design -> build -> backend -> test -> diff -> entrepreneur -> brand -> launch -> deploy
```

An example: cloning a scheduling app, the kind where you share a link and
people book a time with you.

1. **`/replica-recon`** with the app's URL. It reads the help center, the
   pricing page, the store listing and public walkthroughs, and you click
   through your own account with it. Out comes `replica/recon.md`: 18
   screens, 7 flows (guest books a meeting, host sets availability, guest
   reschedules...), the components, an inferred data model (users, event
   types, availability, bookings) and `features.csv`. The partner
   marketplace is marked out of scope: that is their network, not a feature.
2. **`/replica-architect`** picks Next.js, Postgres, Stripe and Resend, writes
   the schema (with a constraint so two guests can never book the same slot)
   and orders the build: the booking flow end to end first.
3. **`/replica-design`** measures the screenshots into tokens: colour roles,
   type scale, 8px spacing, the date picker and slot button specs. Open
   icons, an open font, your own words.
4. **`/replica-build`** builds the shell, then the booking flow, then every
   screen with all its states, ticking off `features.csv` as it goes.
5. **`/replica-backend`** adds sign up, Google Calendar through Google's own
   API with your keys, Stripe for paid bookings, reminder emails.
6. **`/replica-test`** writes a test plan from the 7 flows, Playwright specs
   for the happy paths and edge cases (time zones, a slot taken mid-booking,
   double submit), and logs bugs by severity until no S1 or S2 is open.
7. **`/replica-diff`** scores it. Features 86, all must-haves done, booking
   page layout 91. Missing: round-robin for teams, the website embed.
8. **`/replica-entrepreneur`** reads 140 real reviews across the App Store,
   G2, Capterra and Reddit. Top complaints: per-seat price jumps, no text
   reminders, guests confused by time zones. Each with counts and linked
   quotes. Fix plan: flat pricing, SMS reminders, a time zone confirm step.
   Angle: booking links for small teams that hate per-seat pricing.
9. **`/replica-brand`** names it (with the trademark and domain checks to
   run), gives it a new palette, a logo brief and a voice, then sweeps the
   codebase until nothing of the original is left.
10. **`/replica-launch`** writes the landing page around the angle, sets
    pricing against the original's public page, and lints the store listing.
11. **`/replica-deploy`** runs the preflight (tests, parity, sweep, listing),
    sets up production, gives you the DNS records for your domain, and ships
    it when you say go.

You can also run any one on its own. `/replica-entrepreneur` on an app you
are only thinking about cloning is a good way to find out if you should.

## The tools

Six of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.

```bash
python3 replica-diff/imgdiff.py original.png clone.png --out diff.png   # layout diff, ignores colour
python3 replica-diff/parity.py replica/features.csv                     # parity score + missing list
python3 replica-entrepreneur/reviews.py replica/reviews.csv             # what users hate, ranked, linked
python3 replica-design/contrast.py replica/design/tokens.json           # WCAG contrast on your tokens
python3 replica-brand/sweep.py . --avoid "Original App"                 # anything of the original left?
python3 replica-launch/listing.py replica/launch/listing.json           # store limits + copycat checks
```

**`imgdiff.py`** reads PNGs with no libraries, turns both screenshots into
edge maps and compares where things are, so your new colours do not count
against you. It tells you which regions differ, in the original's pixels.

**`parity.py`** weights must, should and could, counts partial as half, and
never scores what you left out on purpose or what you added. Missing
must-haves means not shippable, and it says so.

**`reviews.py`** drops every review without a link. Every quote it prints is
copied from a row you gave it, with that row's URL. Themes with under three
reviews or one source are marked thin.

**`sweep.py`** finds the original's name, domain and colours anywhere in your
code, including inside identifiers like `OriginalAppEmbed`, and blocks the
deploy until it is clean.

**`listing.py`** checks App Store and Google Play limits, ranking claims in
the title, wasted keyword characters, and the original's name anywhere in
your listing.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Fine print

**It rebuilds functionality and UX patterns, clean-room style.** It studies
what the app does and how people move through it, then writes everything
fresh. It never copies the target's source code, proprietary assets, logos,
trademarks, copy or private APIs.

**It only reads what you are allowed to read.** Public pages and your own
account. It never scrapes behind a login or against a site's terms, never
logs into anyone else's account, and never gets past a paywall. If your
account's terms forbid using it to build a competitor, it says so and sticks
to public sources.

**It always rebrands before launch.** New name, new palette, new logo, new
words. `/replica-deploy` will not ship until the sweep is clean.

**"Clone any app" means the features and the flow.** Not the content, the
network or the licences an app owns. You can rebuild a music app's player,
playlists and sharing. You cannot clone its catalogue.

**No guarantee of a "perfect" clone.** Results depend on how complex the app
is. A booking tool is weeks. A spreadsheet engine is not. `/replica-recon`
sizes it honestly before you start, and `/replica-diff` gives you a real
number, not a vibe.

**The Entrepreneur never makes things up.** No invented reviews, quotes or
numbers. Every claim has a link, and the sample size is stated.

**Check before you sell.** Run the trademark checks `/replica-brand` lists,
read the terms of anything you used, and talk to a lawyer before launch if
there is money on the line. This is not legal advice.

## Files

```
replica-recon/         SKILL.md, recon-map.md, features.csv (the matrix template)
replica-architect/     SKILL.md, architecture.md
replica-design/        SKILL.md, tokens.json, contrast.py
replica-build/         SKILL.md
replica-backend/       SKILL.md
replica-test/          SKILL.md, test-plan.md, bug-report.md, e2e.example.spec.ts
replica-diff/          SKILL.md, imgdiff.py, parity.py
replica-entrepreneur/  SKILL.md, reviews.py, themes.json
replica-brand/         SKILL.md, sweep.py
replica-launch/        SKILL.md, listing.py, listing.example.json
replica-deploy/        SKILL.md, preflight.md
tests/                 the tests for every tool
```

Your own files live in `replica/` in your project. The skills read each
other's.

## Credit

Made by Jake Schincariol, [opusjake.ai](https://opusjake.ai). Siblings:
[Arena](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/arena-skill),
[X](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/x-agent-skill),
[LinkedIn](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill),
[Instagram](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill).

## License

MIT. Take it, change it, ship it.

title: marcelodosreis/sassy
author: marcelodosreis
body:
Sassy

Welcome to **Sassy**, a powerful template generator designed to accelerate the development of Micro-SaaS applications. Built with **Next.js 15**, **TypeScript**, **TailwindCSS**, **Supabase**, and **Stripe**, Sassy provides a robust foundation for building subscription-based services with integrated authentication, subscription management, and payment processing. | **Feature** | **Status** | |-----------------------------------------|------------| | OAuth Authentication (Google, FB, Twitter) | ✅ | | Subscription & Billing (Stripe) | ✅ | | Free Trial Periods (Stripe) | ✅ | | Billing Portal (Stripe) | ✅ | | Webhooks for Stripe Events | ✅ | | Subscriptions & Payments API Routes | ✅ | | User Authentication (Supabase) | ✅ | | E-Mail (Mailgun) | ✅ | | Personalized Dashboard | ✅ | | Responsive Design + Landing Page | ✅ | | Logs & Monitoring (Datadog) | ✅ | You can learn more about the other features by visiting the following documentation page: [Sassy Documentation](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/develop/docs). We are constantly improving Sassy with new features to make it even more powerful. You can find the current roadmap and planned features on our [Feature Roadmap](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/develop/docs/feature-roadmap.md) ## Architecture and Structure Sassy's architecture is designed to streamline the rapid development of Micro-SaaS applications by providing essential features like user authentication, subscription management, and seamless payment processing. The project structure is clean and organized to help developers get started quickly while maintaining flexibility and scalability. ### Project Structure: ```bash src/ ├── app/ # Main logic and core functionality of the application ├── components/ # Reusable UI components ├── constants/ # Global constants and configurations ├── contexts/ # React contexts for global state management ├── hooks/ # Custom React hooks ├── libs/ # Third-party libraries and utilities ├── pages/ # Next.js pages corresponding to routes │ └── api/ # API routes for backend functionality ├── services/ # External API integrations and services ├── styles/ # TailwindCSS configuration and custom styles ├── utils/ # Utility functions and helpers └── middleware.ts # Middleware for request processing ``` ### Integration with Supabase and Stripe: - **Supabase** is used for user authentication and real-time database management. The `subscriptions` table is created to store subscription-related data for each user. - **Stripe** is integrated to handle payment processing and subscription plan management. ### SQL Script for Creating the `subscriptions` Table in Supabase: ```sql CREATE TABLE subscriptions ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, stripe_subscription_id TEXT UNIQUE, plan TEXT CHECK (plan IN ('free', 'starter', 'creator', 'pro')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free', status TEXT CHECK (status IN ('active', 'canceled', 'past_due', 'incomplete', 'trialing')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', current_period_start TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, current_period_end TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() ); ``` > **Note:** Since subscription data is sensitive, ensure that **Row Level Security (RLS)** is disabled for the `subscriptions` table. ### Environment Configuration: The environment variables are configured to integrate Sassy with Supabase and Stripe. Make sure to update the values accordingly. ```env NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_URL= NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY= NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL= NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_APPLICATION_ID= NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_CLIENT_TOKEN= SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY= STRIPE_SECRET_KEY= STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET= DATADOG_SECRET_KEY= MAILGUN_SECRET_KEY= MAILGUN_SECRET_DOMAIN= ``` > **Note:** Replace the above values with your own Supabase and Stripe keys. ## Key Features - **Authentication with Supabase:** Utilize Supabase for user authentication, providing a secure and scalable login system. - **Subscription Management with Stripe:** Easily manage different subscription plans, handle payments, and track user subscriptions with Stripe integration. - **Responsive Design with TailwindCSS:** The application uses TailwindCSS for styling, ensuring a modern and responsive design out of the box. - **Built-in API Routes:** Ready-to-use API routes for managing subscriptions, payments, and user data. - **OAuth Support:** The app supports OAuth login via **Google**, **Facebook**, and **Twitter**, providing users with a seamless authentication experience. --- ## Webhook Listener for Stripe To handle incoming webhooks from Stripe (such as subscription updates, payment failures, etc.), Sassy includes a script for listening to Stripe webhooks: ```bash pnpm stripe:listen ``` This script connects your local environment to Stripe and listens for events like **invoice.payment_succeeded**, **invoice.payment_failed**, and more. It will automatically trigger the corresponding handler in your application to process the events. > **Note:** When using this in your development environment, make sure you have the Stripe secret key and webhook secret configured in your `.env.local` file. --- ## OAuth Authentication Sassy comes with built-in OAuth authentication support for popular platforms such as **Google**, **Facebook**, and **Twitter**. The authentication flow is fully integrated with Supabase, ensuring a secure and seamless experience for users. ### Dependencies: - OAuth SDKs for Google, Facebook, and Twitter to provide login functionality. With **OAuth**, users can authenticate with their preferred social media accounts, reducing friction in the signup/login process. OAuth tokens are securely managed by Supabase, and user data is synchronized across both Supabase and your application. > **Note:** The OAuth login functionality is already set up and fully supported out of the box. If you're using different authentication providers, you can easily extend this functionality by following the Supabase OAuth documentation. --- ## Setup Instructions ### 1. Install Dependencies Ensure that you have **pnpm** installed. If not, install it globally: ```bash npm install -g pnpm ``` Then, install the project dependencies: ```bash pnpm install ``` ### 2. Set Up Environment Variables Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory of the project and add the necessary environment variables (as provided in the **Environment Configuration** section). ### 3. Run the Development Server Once the environment is set up, start the development server: ```bash pnpm dev ``` The application will be available at `http://localhost:3000`. ### 4. Database Configuration To set up your Supabase project, run the provided SQL script to create the `subscriptions` table in your Supabase database. ### 5. Stripe Integration Make sure your Stripe API keys are correctly set up. You can test the payment processing using Stripe’s test keys in a sandbox environment. --- ## Development vs Production Environments For **development** and **production**, Sassy uses separate Supabase projects to ensure a clean and isolated environment. This allows you to safely test changes in the development environment without affecting live data in production. > **Note:** Ensure that you configure your `.env.local` with the correct Supabase project URL and keys for each environment. --- ## Conclusion Sassy provides a solid foundation for developing subscription-based Micro-SaaS applications. By leveraging the power of **Next.js**, **Supabase**, **Stripe**, **OAuth**, and **TailwindCSS**, you can rapidly build and deploy secure and scalable applications. Whether you're just starting a new SaaS product or iterating on an existing idea, Sassy makes it easy to focus on what matters most: delivering value to your users. --- For more information on integrating **Stripe**, **Supabase**, and **OAuth**, refer to the official documentation: - [Stripe Documentation](https://stripe.com/docs) - [Supabase Documentation](https://supabase.com/docs) - [OAuth Integration Guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-helpers/oauth) - [Sassy Integration with Datadog](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/main/docs/datadog.md)
